newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis firm, retail perks up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis firm, retail perks up.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices in early afternoon trade on Monday firmed around one-eighth of a point, responding to stronger Treasuries as well as some reawakened interest from individual investors.

"Retail's been poking their head up a little bit, they're running from the stock market...So we're getting a look now, but we're not knocking it dead," a trader said, cautioning that there still was no groundswell in sight.

For the past 18 months or so, stronger equity markets have siphoned off much of retail investors' cash, slicing into purchases of municipals, but the stock market's recent correction might be starting to alter this pattern.

"We're actually trading some bonds today, not at improved levels, or if improved, I would say very slightly, I would be more in the one-eighth camp," the trader added, disputing views that prices had climbed as much as one-quarter of a point. Traders noted that Monday's activity looked brisk in part because Friday was particularly slow, due to the market's recent retreat.

The market also was looking ahead to one of the biggest new sales calenders this year, with offerings expected to total $4.5 billion in 120 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $3.1 billion in 49 sales, with a $900 million New York City deal on Wednesday, that will be sold through Smith Barney Inc, topping the the list.

The city on Friday got off to a fairly solid start during the first day of the retail presale period, which ends at noon on Tuesday, drawing $134 million of orders. It typically places from $150 million to $200 million of orders with individual investors, before the bonds' prices are finalized during the institutional sales period.
On the competitive side, a $307 million Georgia deal on Tuesday was the largest one scheduled.
Another factor buoying fixed income markets was the stronger dollar, which hit a fresh 50-month high of 125.81 yen.

Traders said the seed for this rally was planted last Friday when Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin "took the dollar off the table" after he denounced the use of currency rates to manipulate trade accounts. The gap betweeen U.S. interest rates and Japanese rates also was expected to remain wide after the recent monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve.
Actively traded municipal bonds included Alabama Housing Financing Authority Single Family Mortgage Revenues of October 2021, which pay a six percent coupon, and were bid at 98-5/8, up one-eighth.
And Florida Ports Financing Commission Revenues of June 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were offered at 5.97 percent, NET, down two basis points.
The MOB spread stood at plus 144 ticks. The June Treasury bond contract was up 18/32 at 107-18/32, while the June municipal bond futures rose 11 ticks to 112-2/32.
